chapters.title: The core pattern: token, headers, REST

takeaways: Calling Microsoft Graph directly with Invoke-RestMethod removes module load times, dependency conflicts and the lag between new Graph features and module releases.
Use device code for local testing, client credentials with a certificate for unattended automation, and managed identity wherever the workload runs in Azure.
Production Graph scripts need paging via nextLink, retry with backoff on throttling, a dry-run flag, logging of request IDs and a token audience that matches Graph.
hook: PowerShell scripts built on MSOnline, AzureAD or heavy Graph modules break on Linux runners, containers and CI/CD. This episode shows admins and automation engineers the module-free token, headers and REST pattern for Microsoft Graph, three auth flows and three enterprise demos for Intune cleanup, onboarding and compliance remediation.
